mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.5% indicates a weak labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.5%) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 94.0) indicates an accelerating economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5 AND INDPRO < 94.0.

mechanism_narrative: During the early phase of a post-recession recovery, rising housing starts (HOUST > 500) signal improving consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during early post-recession recovery when HOUST > 500.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 94.0) relative to the previous month signals a contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate profits and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 94.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.0% signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS > 370,000 million dollars) indicate robust consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 370,000.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 219.0) signals increasing price pressures, prompting the Fed to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 219.0.
